fact.1: Ducks' feet don't freeze: warm and cold blood vessels run side by side, so they can stand on ice.
fact.2: Ducks can sleep with one eye open, keeping half of the brain awake to watch out.
fact.3: A duck's quack does echo. The myth that it doesn't was tested and busted.
fact.4: Ducklings follow the first moving thing they see after hatching. It is called imprinting.
fact.5: A duck keeps its feathers waterproof with oil from a gland near its tail, spread on while preening.
fact.6: Migrating ducks can fly at around 60–80 km/h.
fact.7: Ducks have three eyelids: the third one is see-through and sweeps across the eye like a wiper.
fact.8: The loud classic "quack" comes from female mallards. Males make a softer, raspy sound.
fact.9: Ducks see more colors than we do, ultraviolet included.
fact.10: A group of ducks resting on the water is called a raft.
fact.11: After nesting, many ducks lose all their flight feathers at once and cannot fly for a few weeks.
fact.12: The hard tip of a duck's bill is called the "nail". It helps dig up food.
fact.13: With eyes on the sides of its head, a duck sees almost all the way round.
fact.14: Rubber duck debugging: explain your code line by line to a duck, and the bug often shows itself.
